sample_unit: decision-tree model analysis (no patient sample reported)

links.outcome: Fairness of UTICalc across racial groups by prediction metric versus outcome-based expected utility parity
links.effect: Revised UTICalc improved equal opportunity (true positive rate parity) but did not improve expected utility parity, so prediction-based and outcome-based fairness diverged.
links.quote: Our results show that the revised UTICalc model did not improve an outcome-based fairness metric, namely, expected utility parity.

unlisted_practices: Evaluating fairness of clinical prediction models with a decision-theoretic framework integrating patient outcome utilities (expected utility parity)

screen.reason: The study empirically evaluates a real-world deployed clinical predictive tool (UTICalc) and tests the impact of model revision for fairness metrics versus decision-theoretic patient outcome utility parity.

primary.practice: outcome-based vs prediction-based algorithmic fairness evaluation
